addresses.name: CCallAllyAction::IsValid
addresses.comment: Slot 13 of a call to arms (actor +0x8 the caller, recipient +0x10 the ally called, Versus +0x28 the enemy). In order: the recipient's status towards Versus has no war; the caller's has one (W); not (Versus is in a real faction - its CFaction slot 7 - and in the recipient's faction); the recipient is not in W's attackers (+0x2C, by id) nor its defenders (+0x3C, CountryTagVector_Contains); and **W's call map (+0x74, WarCallMap_Subscript) holds 0 for the recipient, or the action is not a PROPOSE** - so a second call to a country already called and unanswered in this war is invalid, while the answers to it pass. The subscript inserts a 0 entry as a side effect. Two bare `ret`s, 0xA2A3FF and 0xA2A4D0. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md, section B.1.
addresses.evidence: Read off the disassembly 0xA2A3C0-0xA2A4D0: the war tests at 0xA2A3F1 and 0xA2A41C, the faction slot 7 call at 0xA2A438 and the faction compare at 0xA2A469, the attacker loop at 0xA2A480, Contains on +0x3C at 0xA2A49A, `lea eax,[edi+0x74]` and `call 0xA526D0` at 0xA2A4AE/0xA2A4B5, then `cmp [eax],0` / `cmp [esi+0x18],0`. Wrong if 0xA526D0 were not a std::map<int,int> subscript - it is byte for byte the shape of 0x421340, a red-black-tree lower bound with key at node +0xC and value at +0x10, inserting {key, 0} when absent.
addresses.revises: Confidence raised from inferred; the unread gate 0xA526D0 is named - the war's call map at +0x74, written 1 by Apply on a PROPOSE and 0 on either answer.

addresses.name: CCallAllyAction::IsSelectable
addresses.comment: Slot 14, what greys the row. In order: actor != recipient; the caller is at war with Versus (W); not (Versus in a real faction shared with the recipient); **W's `limited` byte (+0x70) set - a call to arms can be chosen only in a limited war**; influence (or 100.000 under g_UnlimitedDiploInfluence) >= CALLALLY_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0x1C, 1.0 in Their Finest Hour); both sides of W have at least one country. Then the puppet rule: where the recipient is no subject, **only the first country of a side (attackers[0] or defenders[0]) may call**; where the recipient's overlord is the caller, the caller needs only to be in W; where it has another overlord, the caller must lead its side and that overlord must already be on it. Last, false where the recipient has a NAP with any real country (not id 0, not REB) on the side the caller fights. Bare `ret`. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md, section B.1.
addresses.evidence: Read off the disassembly from 0xA2A4E0: `cmp byte ptr [ebx+0x70],0; je false` at 0xA2A58B, the define at diplomacy +0x1C read at 0xA2A5B8, the two side-size tests at 0xA2A5EB/0xA2A605, the leader test on attackers[0]/defenders[0] from 0xA2A60E; the puppet branches and the NAP loop as decompiled, checked against the calls to CountryTagVector_Contains. Wrong if +0x70 meant full war: CDeclareWarAction::Apply writes 1 to it only when the action's value is 0 (0xA12807-0xA1280C), and the Declare Limited War row is the value-0 one.

addresses.name: CCallAllyAction::Apply
addresses.comment:
CCallAllyAction slot 7, one holder (vftable 0x15FB6F4). 0xA27BA0 to the bare `ret` at 0xA29D33, 12 int3, then slot 11 at 0xA29D40; the `ret` at 0xA284CE is an arm of the same frame. Parties: actor (+0x8) the caller, recipient (+0x10) the ally called, Versus (+0x28) the enemy; W = the caller's war with Versus. It first builds the message variables (the player's standard list, ACTOR, RECIPIENT, MESSENGER = MESSAGE_HEAD_CHAN, VERSUS), then by `type`:

**PROPOSE (0)**: W's call map (+0x74) [recipient] = 1; then, **only where `value` is 0**, the caller's diplo_influence -= CALLALLY_INFLUENCE_COST (diplomacy +0x1C), clamped at 0. A value-1 call costs nothing.

**ACCEPT (2)**: call map [recipient] = 0. On the recipient's status towards Versus: the alliance, the guarantee and the NAP are each Deactivated (slot 11), unlinked (CDiplomacy_RemoveRelation) and deleted, and an undeclared war is taken out of the game state's list at +0xC10 and deleted. Which side: the side the caller is on (attackers if CountryTagVector_Contains(+0x2C, caller), else defenders). A flag `lead` is set where the side's first country (attackers[0], or defenders[0], or the caller where defenders is empty) owns fewer provinces (+0xCF8) than the recipient, cleared where the recipient is a subject, and set where the recipient is the caller's overlord; it is CWar::AddAttacker/AddDefender's third argument. SetMilitaryAccess(0) on both directions between the recipient and Versus. Then CWar::AddDefender(W, 1, lead, recipient) - or CWar::AddAttacker(W, 1, lead, recipient) and, where the recipient is not the caller's puppet, AddCasusBelli(recipient, Versus) followed at once by CDiplomacyStatus::ClearCasusBelli on the same status: the new type-0 casus belli and every other one is unlinked from the status while the objects stay in the relation list. ChangeRelation(Versus, recipient, -WARDEC_WAR_DIPLOMACY_HIT) (-100); OnDiplomacyChanged on caller, recipient and Versus; TARGETLIST = the names of the side the recipient now fights, ', '-joined. A branch on the recipient's +0xDE4 (the faction rule ALLIANCE_GUARANTEE, which nothing writes) would make, for each member of the recipient's faction not already a defender, a CCallAllyAction (recipient calls member against Versus) at ACCEPT and Execute it at once - dead. Messages: caller played - sound diplomaticsuccess and MILALLHONOUR; recipient played - WEMILALLHONOUR where `value` is set, else FACTIONWAROFF (joined the attackers) or FACTIONWARDEF with VICTIM = Versus and FACTION = the caller's faction name; anybody else - OTHERMILALLHONOUR. Then DeleteAreaGroups (0x7FFF0), RebuildAreaGroups, DeleteSupplyGroups (0x807F0), RebuildSupplyGroups.

**DECLINE (1)**: call map [recipient] = 0; ChangeRelation(recipient, caller, ALLIANCE_REJECT_RELATION_CHANGE) (diplomacy +0x44, -50); AddCasusBelli(caller, recipient) - a type-0 casus belli for the caller on the refuser; **the caller-recipient alliance, where there is one, is Deactivated, unlinked and deleted**. TARGETLIST = the side the caller fights. Messages **only where an alliance was broken**: caller played - sound diplomaticfailure and MILALLDISHONOUR; recipient played - WEMILALLDISHONOUR; else OTHERMILALLDISHONOUR.

Any other `type` returns after the variables. Execute exempts this class from the seven-day cooldown write. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md, section B.1.
addresses.evidence: Read arm by arm on the disassembly (scratch apply.asm, 0xA27BA0-0xA29D33): the type dispatch at 0xA2840A/0xA284CF/0xA2962B; the PROPOSE map write `lea eax,[ecx+0x74]; call 0x421340; mov [eax],1` at 0xA28460-0xA2846C and `cmp [edi+0x24],bl; jne exit` at 0xA28472 before the charge at 0xA284A2; ACCEPT's three relation removals at 0xA28525-0xA2870A (+0x14, +0x1C, +0x28) and the undeclared war at 0xA2870E; the side test at 0xA287C7, the province compare at 0xA28827, the subject and overlord tests at 0xA28840/0xA2886C; SetMilitaryAccess at 0xA28891/0xA288C4; AddAttacker at 0xA288F5, the overlord test at 0xA28922, AddCasusBelli at 0xA2893C (holder pushed = countries[recipient], target ECX = &Versus) and ClearCasusBelli at 0xA28958 on countries[recipient]->diplomacy[Versus]; AddDefender at 0xA2897D; ChangeRelation at 0xA289C6; the +0xDE4 test at 0xA28CA0; the message keys at 0xA28F52, 0xA290A2, 0xA29343, 0xA29406, 0xA294F7 with the value test at 0xA2908B; DECLINE's map write at 0xA29682, ChangeRelation(EDI = recipient, ECX = &caller) at 0xA296B5, AddCasusBelli(caller, &recipient) at 0xA296D7, the alliance removal at 0xA29704-0xA2977B and the message gate `cmp [esp+0x26],bl; je` at 0xA29986. Wrong if 0x421340 were not a map subscript (its shape is identical to WarCallMap_Subscript's).
addresses.revises: Confidence raised from inferred; read whole. Corrections: the influence is charged only for a value-0 call; joining as an attacker does not discard the casus belli the ally held - it gives the ally a type-0 one on the enemy and then unlinks all of them from that status; declining also breaks the caller-recipient alliance and only then raises the DISHONOUR messages; the next call this body manufactures sits behind +0xDE4, which nothing writes, so honouring a call never calls anyone else.

addresses.name: WarCallMap_Subscript
addresses.comment: **std::map<int,int>::operator[]**: MSVC's red-black tree, head at map+4, node key at +0xC and value at +0x10, `_Isnil` at +0x15; the lower bound is walked and, where the key is absent, a {key, 0} node is inserted (0x542EF0, 0x422250) - so a lookup creates the entry. Its one caller hands it CWar +0x74, the war's call map, from CCallAllyAction::IsValid at 0xA2A4B5. A second instantiation of the same template as IntIntMap_Subscript (0x21340), compiled in another unit with other registers and not folded. Class-free: a template body, not a CWar method. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md, section B.1.
addresses.evidence: Decoded 0xA526D0-0xA52746, two bare `ret`s; EAX is the map (`mov esi,eax; mov ecx,[esi+4]`), EDX the key pointer (`mov ecx,[edx]`), the return is the value's address (`lea eax,[ebx+0x10]` or `add eax,0x10`). Wrong if the value were wider than a dword - the insert writes {key, 0} as two dwords at [ebp-8]/[ebp-4].

addresses.name: IntIntMap_Subscript

Twelve direct callers; three are CCallAllyAction::Apply's writes to the war's call map (CWar +0x74) at 0xA28467 (=1), 0xA2851E and 0xA2967D (=0). See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md, section B.1.

addresses.name: CWarGoal_IsAvailable
addresses.comment: **Whether a war goal can still be chosen.** W = actor->diplomacy[recipient]->war. False where the type is not real (slot 7). False where allowed_countries has conditions (+0x180) and no third country is set. Where allowed_regions has conditions (+0x100) and no region is set: true where some province of some region of g_CMap (all regions, useForPeace not asked) passes allowed_regions in {province, THIS = actor} (FROM empty) and either there is no war or W's goals of the actor hold no goal equal in type, actor, recipient, third country and that region. Where neither, true unless the same goal is already in W. Bare `ret`. Callers: the war-goal dialog's three lists, CCountry::GetMaxNeutralityForWarWith and its tooltip twin. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md, section B.4.

addresses.name: CWarGoal::BuildSetupText
addresses.comment: A war goal's description, the war-goal dialog's Description and the war-goal row's delayed tooltip. Empty where the type is null or not real. Otherwise the text of `<type key>_setup` (puppet_setup 'Install a loyal government in $RECIPIENT$') with ACTOR and RECIPIENT = '§Y' + the country's name + '§W'; then the text's own replacement keys are scanned for THIRD and STATE. Else '§W' + the rendered text. Three callers: the war-goal row's delayed tooltip and two in the war-goal dialog. 0x479D40, three `ret 8`, the last at 0x47A79B. See reversing/findings/FINDINGS-diplomacyview.md and reversing/findings/FINDINGS-war.md section B.4.
